ei.subject: 영어2
ei.title: Microbes and Health — The Hidden Heroes Inside Us

fullPassage:
A human being has about 10 trillion human cells, but there are also other tiny creatures living in the human body. These creatures are clusters of bacteria in different parts of the body, such as on the surface or in the deep layers of the skin, in the mouth and the nose, and in the lungs and the stomach. But the greatest number of bacteria, about 100 trillion that weigh up to 2 kg, reside in the gut. This may sound somewhat frightening, but these bacteria have a crucial and positive influence on our health. The first scientist who paid attention to these microbes in the gut and their importance was Ilya Mechinikov, who won the Nobel Prize in 1908 for his studies on the immune system. He was living in Paris in the late 19th century when thousands of people were suffering from cholera, a disease that was sweeping the European continent. As a scientist, Mechinikov was naturally driven to study this disease, which eventually led him to eat food containing the cholera bacteria. Remarkably, he didn't get sick. Intrigued, he decided to increase his sample size and recruited a colleague to do the same. The colleague didn't get sick either. But when he tested on another colleague, the poor man became critically ill and almost died. What made them react to the same disease in different ways? By studying cholera under the microscope, Mechinikov found that certain species of bacteria from the human gut supported and stimulated the cholera's growth, while other species prevented it. After further study, he realized that our gut bacteria were essential for human health, and that the right balance of microbes inside of us could help prevent disease. Sadly, this view was not widely accepted at the time and was eventually forgotten after Mechinikov died in 1916.

A decade later, antibiotics were discovered. Antibiotics have saved countless lives by giving doctors and scientists the means to kill harmful germs that infect wounds, cause deadly diseases, and spread through food. However, as time has passed, the miraculous power of antibiotics has caused some doctors to use them too much. Moreover, people have come to see all germs as threats to good health, and as a result, they have done their best to keep their bodies clean of them. A war has been waged on microbes, and people have spent almost a century trying to kill them. Unfortunately, this attitude has had harmful effects on health, resulting in a rise in allergies and immune deficiencies.

Fortunately, scientists are beginning to see the relationship between microbes and the human body in a new light. According to recent studies, thousands of species of microbes in the gut have different functions, and good health is incredibly dependent upon the well-being of these numerous and diverse microbes. By occupying our bodies first, they prevent harmful germs from growing there. Therefore, people with a healthy bacterial community may remain unaffected by slightly infected food, but those with fewer or unbalanced microbes may suffer from food poisoning. They also facilitate our immune system by distinguishing between good substances that should be allowed into our bodies and harmful ones that should be rejected. Therefore, having insufficient germs or losing important ones leads to various health problems. Some microbes help the stomach digest some vegetables and milk. If they are absent, it is difficult to absorb certain vegetables and milk, which eventually leads to an unbalanced diet and poorer health. Other bacteria help the body produce vitamins B and K, as well as important amino acids. Some microbes in the gut determine whether particular drugs are toxic to the liver and whether or not other drugs will work to combat a heart condition. Other microbes regulate the appetite hormone, which makes a person feel full or hungry. Losing these microbes may result in increased body fat. One recent study found that transplanting a lean mouse's gut bacteria into an overweight mouse's stomach made the overweight mouse lose weight. Similarly, doing the reverse made the lean mouse gain weight.

Some researchers who have realized the crucial role of microbes are trying to apply this knowledge to cure people. Instead of using antibiotics, they have found that introducing or increasing the necessary germs that the person lacks can cure some diseases. For example, there were people who had a terrible form of diarrhea, so they had to go to the bathroom up to 20 times a day. These people had not been helped by antibiotic therapy. Researchers transplanted some of the good microbes from a healthy donor into these patients' guts. One day after they received their transplant, all their symptoms cleared up and the diarrhea vanished. They were essentially healthy again. The bacterial community in their own guts came to resemble the donor's bacterial community. Given this knowledge, nutritionists suggest the following ways to keep our guts healthy. One of the easiest ways to do this is through our food. Good microbes can be found in many of the foods we eat and whatever else gets to our mouths. By eating foods that contain beneficial bacteria, such as yogurt, gimchi, and natto, or choosing a diet packed with good, fresh nutrients, such as garlic, onions, and unprocessed grains rich in fiber, we can cultivate good microbes. Of course, it is also important to protect the germs that already exist in our bodies by avoiding processed food. Heavily processed foods such as frozen food, packaged snacks, and canned food not only lack beneficial bacteria but also contain chemicals that damage the good microbes in our guts. Another way to increase beneficial microbes is to spend more time in nature. Places with diverse life forms, such as woods, beaches, parks, or even small farms and gardens, are abundant with diverse bacteria that germ-free urban environments lack. In addition, we should use antibiotics wisely; we must use them much less frequently. Although antibiotics play a crucial role in keeping us healthy by eliminating dangerous germs, they cannot tell good bacteria from bad ones. Therefore, whenever we use antibiotics, we inevitably damage beneficial bacteria as well as the harmful bacteria that we want to get rid of. If we can affect microbes and they can affect our bodies, it makes little sense to talk about the two separately. Maybe it is time to stop thinking of microbes and ourselves as different beings. We need to start thinking of the microbes in our guts as a part of our bodies, like the blood cells and the neurons, and take care of them just as we take care of our skin and our teeth.

ⓒ paying — ❌ who paid가 올바름 (관계절의 동사, 과거시제)
ⓓ who — ✅ 계속적 관계대명사, 주격
det.tip: 🔑 관계절 내의 동사 시제는 주절과 일치시켜야 합니다. was → paid (과거). paying은 진행형이므로 was paying이어야 하지만 원문은 단순 과거 paid.

(A)[Intriguing / Intrigued], he decided to increase his sample size. What made them (B)[react / to react] to the same disease in different ways?

det.ref: [원문] Intrigued, he decided to increase his sample size. / What made them react to the same disease in different ways? [해석] 흥미를 느낀 그는 표본 크기를 늘리기로 했다. / 무엇이 그들을 같은 질병에 다르게 반응하게 했는가?
det.correct: ✅ ② (A) Intrigued – (B) react: (A) he가 흥미를 '느끼는' 것이므로 과거분사 Intrigued(감정의 수동). (B) make + O + 동사원형 (사역동사 구문).
wrongs: ① (A) Intriguing – (B) react: 사람이 흥미를 '유발하는' 것이 아니라 '느끼는' 것 ❌
③ (A) Intriguing – (B) to react: 두 가지 모두 틀림 ❌
④ (A) Intrigued – (B) to react: make는 to부정사를 취하지 않음 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 감정 분사: -ed(감정을 느끼는 사람), -ing(감정을 유발하는 것). make + O + 동사원형 (사역동사).

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] people have come to see all germs as threats to good health. [해석] 사람들은 모든 세균을 건강에 대한 위협으로 보게 되었다.
det.correct:
① miraculous — ✅ '기적적인', 항생제의 놀라운 힘
② allies — ❌ 원문은 threats(위협). 사람들이 세균을 '동맹'이 아닌 '위협'으로 본다는 맥락. 전쟁을 벌인다는 뒤 문장과 연결.
③ kill — ✅ '죽이다', 미생물을 죽이려 노력
④ harmful — ✅ '해로운', 건강에 해로운 영향
det.tip: 🔑 threats(위협) ↔ allies(동맹). 세균에 대해 전쟁을 벌이고 죽이려 한다는 맥락 → 세균을 '위협'으로 보는 것이 자연스럽다.

questions.passage: Of course, it is also important to protect the germs that already exist in our bodies by avoiding processed food. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] diverse bacteria that germ-free urban environments lack. [해석] 무균 도시 환경에 없는 다양한 박테리아.
det.correct:
① chemicals — ✅ '화학물질', 가공식품에 포함된 유해 물질
② damage — ✅ '손상시키다', 화학물질이 좋은 미생물을 손상
③ abundant — ✅ '풍부한', 자연에는 다양한 박테리아가 풍부
④ rural — ❌ 원문은 urban(도시의). 무균 환경은 '도시'이지 '시골'이 아님. 시골은 오히려 다양한 생명체가 있는 곳.
det.tip: 🔑 urban(도시의) ↔ rural(시골의). 무균(germ-free) 환경은 도시(urban)에 해당. 시골은 자연과 가까워 박테리아가 풍부.

questions.passage: Although antibiotics play a crucial role in keeping us healthy by ①<u>eliminating</u> dangerous germs, they cannot ②<u>tell</u> good bacteria from bad ones. Therefore, whenever we use antibiotics, we inevitably damage ③<u>beneficial</u> bacteria as well as the harmful bacteria that we want to get ④<u>close</u> of.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.

det.ref: [원문] the harmful bacteria that we want to get rid of. [해석] 우리가 제거하고 싶은 해로운 박테리아.
det.correct:
① eliminating — ✅ '제거하는', 위험한 세균을 제거
② tell — ✅ 'tell A from B = A와 B를 구별하다', 좋은 균과 나쁜 균 구별 불가
③ beneficial — ✅ '유익한', 유익한 박테리아도 손상
④ close — ❌ 원문은 rid. 'get rid of' = 제거하다. 'get close of'는 존재하지 않는 표현.
det.tip:
🔑 get rid of = ~을 제거하다, 없애다. tell A from B = A와 B를 구별하다.
⚠️ get close to(가까이 가다)는 전치사 to를 쓰며, get close of는 틀린 표현.

미생물 이식 후 회복까지 약 한 달이 소요되었다.

questions.passage: By studying cholera under the microscope, Mechinikov found that certain species of bacteria from the human gut supported and stimulated the cholera's growth, while other species prevented it. After further study, he realized that our gut bacteria were essential for human health, and that the right balance of microbes inside of us could help prevent disease. Sadly, this view was not widely accepted at the time and was eventually forgotten after Mechinikov died in 1916.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.ref: [원문] certain species supported cholera's growth / other species prevented it / gut bacteria essential for health / right balance could prevent disease / view not widely accepted / forgotten after death in 1916.
det.correct:
✅ ② 메치니코프의 발견은 당시 과학계에서 널리 인정받았다 — 원문은 정반대. 'not widely accepted'이고 사후 'forgotten'.
❌ ① 일부 장 박테리아는 콜레라의 성장을 촉진했다 — 원문 일치 ✅
❌ ③ 미생물의 올바른 균형이 질병 예방에 도움이 될 수 있다 — 원문 일치 ✅
❌ ④ 메치니코프의 견해는 그가 사망한 후 잊혀졌다 — 원문 일치 ✅
det.tip: 🔑 Sadly, this view was not widely accepted → 널리 인정받지 못했다. '널리 인정받았다'는 원문과 정반대.

ch: 일부 장 박테리아는 콜레라의 성장을 촉진했다.
메치니코프의 발견은 당시 과학계에서 널리 인정받았다.
미생물의 올바른 균형이 질병 예방에 도움이 될 수 있다.
메치니코프의 견해는 그가 1916년 사망한 후 잊혀졌다.

questions.passage: Some microbes help the stomach digest some vegetables and milk. If they are absent, it is difficult to absorb certain vegetables and milk, which eventually leads to an unbalanced diet and poorer health. Other bacteria help the body produce vitamins B and K, as well as important amino acids. Some microbes in the gut determine whether particular drugs are toxic to the liver.
questions.stem:
이 글에 따르면, 미생물이 부재할 경우 빈칸에 들어갈 결과로 가장 적절한 것은?

Without certain microbes, our bodies struggle to __________ key nutrients from food.

det.ref: [원문] If they are absent, it is difficult to absorb certain vegetables and milk. [해석] 미생물이 없으면 특정 채소와 우유를 흡수하기 어렵다.
det.correct:
✅ ① absorb: 미생물이 없으면 영양소를 '흡수'하기 어렵다는 원문의 내용.
❌ ② produce(생산하다) — 미생물이 비타민을 생산하는 것이지 사람이 영양소를 생산하는 것이 아님
❌ ③ eliminate(제거하다) — 영양소를 제거하는 것이 아님
❌ ④ detect(탐지하다) — 영양소를 탐지하는 것이 아님
det.tip: 🔑 absorb = 흡수하다. 미생물이 소화를 도와서 영양소를 흡수할 수 있게 한다.

questions.passage: Fortunately, scientists are beginning to see the relationship between microbes and the human body in a new light. According to recent studies, thousands of species of microbes in the gut have different functions, and good health is incredibly dependent upon the well-being of these numerous and diverse microbes. By occupying our bodies first, they prevent harmful germs from growing there. Therefore, people with a healthy bacterial community may remain unaffected by slightly infected food, but those with fewer or unbalanced microbes may suffer from food poisoning.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

The author implies that the __________ of our microbial ecosystem is more important than simply having a large number of microbes.

det.ref: [원문] good health is incredibly dependent upon the well-being of these numerous and diverse microbes. / those with fewer or unbalanced microbes may suffer [해석] 건강은 이 수많고 다양한 미생물의 안녕에 의존 / 불균형한 미생물을 가진 사람은 고통받을 수 있다.
det.correct:
✅ ③ diversity: 단순히 많은 수가 아닌, '다양성(diversity)'과 '균형'이 중요하다는 것이 핵심. numerous AND diverse, fewer OR unbalanced → 다양성과 균형이 핵심.
❌ ① location(위치) — 미생물의 위치가 아닌 다양성 논의
❌ ② origin(기원) — 미생물의 기원이 아닌 구성의 다양성
❌ ④ temperature(온도) — 온도와 무관
det.tip: 🔑 diverse(다양한) + unbalanced(불균형한)에서 '다양성과 균형'이 핵심 키워드임을 파악.

questions.passage: A human being has about 10 trillion human cells, but there are also other tiny creatures living in the human body. These creatures are clusters of bacteria in different parts of the body. But the greatest number of bacteria, about 100 trillion that weigh up to 2 kg, reside in the gut. This may sound somewhat frightening, but these bacteria have a crucial and positive influence on our health. We need to start thinking of the microbes in our guts as a part of our bodies, like the blood cells and the neurons, and take care of them just as we take care of our skin and our teeth.
questions.stem: 이 글의 제목이 "The Hidden Heroes Inside Us"일 때, "hidden heroes"가 함축하는 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: [제목] Microbes and Health — The Hidden Heroes Inside Us. [원문 맥락] 100조 개의 박테리아가 장에 살며 건강에 결정적인 역할 / 사람들은 미생물을 적으로 봤지만 사실은 도움이 됨 / 몸의 일부로 돌봐야 함.
det.correct:
✅ ② 눈에 보이지 않지만 건강을 지키는 데 결정적 역할을 하는 장 미생물 — hidden(보이지 않는) + heroes(영웅적 역할) = 눈에 안 보이지만 건강에 핵심적인 미생물.
❌ ① 과학자들이 발견하지 못한 새로운 종류의 세균 — hidden이 '발견 안 된'의 의미가 아님
❌ ③ 항생제 속에 숨어 있는 유익한 화학 성분 — 항생제가 아닌 미생물
❌ ④ 체내에서 자연적으로 생성되는 면역 항체 — 항체가 아닌 미생물
det.tip: 🔑 hidden = 눈에 보이지 않는(tiny creatures), heroes = 건강에 결정적 역할(crucial and positive influence). 미생물이 적이 아닌 영웅이라는 역설적 메시지.

ch: 과학자들이 아직 발견하지 못한 미지의 세균 종류
눈에 보이지 않지만 건강을 지키는 데 핵심적인 장 미생물
항생제 속에 숨어 있는 유익한 화학 성분

questions.passage: Some researchers who have realized the crucial role of microbes are trying to apply this knowledge to cure people.
questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

(A) Researchers transplanted some of the good microbes from a healthy donor into these patients' guts. One day after they received their transplant, all their symptoms cleared up and the diarrhea vanished.

(B) Instead of using antibiotics, they have found that introducing or increasing the necessary germs that the person lacks can cure some diseases.

(C) For example, there were people who had a terrible form of diarrhea, so they had to go to the bathroom up to 20 times a day. These people had not been helped by antibiotic therapy.

det.ref: [원문 순서] 연구자들이 미생물로 치료 시도 → (B) 항생제 대신 필요한 세균 도입/증가 → (C) 예를 들어 심한 설사 환자 → (A) 건강한 기증자의 미생물 이식 후 증상 소멸.
det.correct: ✅ ② (B)-(C)-(A): 일반적 발견(B) → 구체적 예시 도입(C: For example) → 치료 결과(A)의 논리적 흐름.
wrongs: ① (A)-(B)-(C): 치료 결과가 먼저 나오면 맥락이 맞지 않음 ❌
③ (C)-(A)-(B): 예시(For example)가 일반론(B)보다 먼저 올 수 없음 ❌
④ (B)-(A)-(C): 예시(For example) 없이 바로 치료로 넘어가면 비약 ❌
det.tip: 🔑 일반론(B: 세균 도입으로 치료) → 예시 도입(C: For example, 설사 환자) → 구체적 치료/결과(A: 이식 후 완치). 'For example'이 (C)에 있으므로 (B) 다음.

questions.passage: ① One of the easiest ways to keep our guts healthy is through our food. ② By eating foods that contain beneficial bacteria, such as yogurt, gimchi, and natto, we can cultivate good microbes. ③ Recent studies have shown that regular physical exercise can improve cardiovascular health and reduce the risk of heart disease. ④ Of course, it is also important to protect the germs that already exist in our bodies by avoiding processed food.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?

det.ref: [글의 흐름] 장 건강 유지법: 음식을 통한 유익균 섭취 → 가공식품 회피. ③번은 운동과 심혈관 건강에 대한 내용으로 장 미생물/음식 주제와 무관.
det.correct:
✅ ③ 최근 연구에 따르면 규칙적인 운동이 심혈관 건강을 개선할 수 있다 — 음식을 통한 장 건강 유지라는 주제에서 벗어난 무관한 문장.
❌ ①②④는 모두 '음식을 통한 장 건강 유지'라는 흐름에 부합.
det.tip: 🔑 글의 흐름: 음식으로 장 건강 유지(①) → 유익균 음식(②) → [무관: 운동+심혈관(③)] → 가공식품 회피(④)

questions.passage: Other microbes regulate the appetite hormone, which makes a person feel full or hungry. Losing these microbes may result in increased body fat. One recent study found that transplanting a lean mouse's gut bacteria into an overweight mouse's stomach made the overweight mouse lose weight. Similarly, doing the reverse made the lean mouse gain weight.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용으로 보아, 아래 진술의 T(True) 또는 F(False)를 올바르게 짝지은 것은?

(가) 미생물은 식욕 호르몬을 조절하는 역할을 한다.
(나) 미생물을 잃으면 체지방이 감소할 수 있다.
(다) 마른 쥐의 장 박테리아를 과체중 쥐에 이식하면 과체중 쥐가 체중을 줄인다.

det.ref: [원문] regulate the appetite hormone(T) / Losing these microbes may result in increased body fat(→ 증가, F) / transplanting lean mouse's bacteria into overweight mouse made it lose weight(T).
det.correct: ✅ ② (가) T — (나) F — (다) T: (가) 식욕 호르몬 조절 → T. (나) 미생물 손실 시 체지방 '증가'이므로 '감소'는 F. (다) 마른 쥐→과체중 쥐 이식 시 체중 감소 → T.
wrongs: ① (가) T — (나) T — (다) T: (나)는 체지방 증가이므로 F ❌
det.tip: 🔑 Losing these microbes → increased body fat (체지방 증가, 감소 아님). 진술을 원문과 정확히 대조!

questions.passage: A decade later, antibiotics were discovered. Antibiotics have saved countless lives by giving doctors and scientists the means to kill harmful germs that infect wounds, cause deadly diseases, and spread through food. However, as time has passed, the miraculous power of antibiotics has caused some doctors to use them too much.
questions.stem:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

The ( __________ ) power of antibiotics led to their overuse by some doctors.

det.ref: [원문] the miraculous power of antibiotics has caused some doctors to use them too much. [해석] 항생제의 기적적인 힘이 일부 의사들이 과용하게 만들었다.
det.tip: 🔑 miraculous = 기적적인, 놀라운. 항생제의 '기적적인' 힘이 남용을 초래.

questions.passage: The bacterial community in their own guts came to resemble the donor's bacterial community. Given this knowledge, nutritionists suggest the following ways to keep our guts healthy. One of the easiest ways to do this is through our food. By eating foods that contain beneficial bacteria, such as yogurt, gimchi, and natto, or choosing a diet packed with good, fresh nutrients, such as garlic, onions, and unprocessed grains rich in fiber, we can cultivate good microbes.
questions.stem:
다음 문장의 괄호 안 단어를 어법에 맞게 고쳐 쓰시오.

By ( eat ) foods that contain beneficial bacteria, we can cultivate good microbes.

det.ref: [원문] By eating foods that contain beneficial bacteria ... we can cultivate good microbes. [해석] 유익한 박테리아가 포함된 음식을 먹음으로써 좋은 미생물을 기를 수 있다.
det.tip: 🔑 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 온다. by + V-ing = '~함으로써'. eat → eating

questions.passage: If we can affect microbes and they can affect our bodies, it makes little sense to talk about the two separately. Maybe it is time to stop thinking of microbes and ourselves as different beings. We need to start thinking of the microbes in our guts as a part of our bodies, like the blood cells and the neurons, and take care of them just as we take care of our skin and our teeth.
questions.stem:
다음 글을 읽고, 주어진 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오.

[조건] ① 주어진 단어를 모두 포함 ② 필요시 어형 변환 ③ 6단어 이내
[보기] make / little / sense / talk

우리말: "둘을 따로 이야기하는 것은 의미가 거의 없다."
→ It ( ________________________________ ) about the two separately.

det.ref: [원문] it makes little sense to talk about the two separately. [해석] 둘을 따로 이야기하는 것은 의미가 거의 없다.
det.tip: 🔑 make little sense = 의미가 거의 없다. It makes little sense to talk = ~하는 것은 의미가 거의 없다.
